sec: Apoplexy treatment and Sheehan syndrome pathophysiology

items.q: What is the mandatory immediate first-line medical intervention for a patient with acute pituitary apoplexy?
opts: 100 mg IV hydrocortisone followed by decompressive surgery
Urgent intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics and lumbar puncture
High-dose intravenous dexamethasone 4 mg every 6 hours only
Emergency thrombolytic therapy with recombinant tPA
items.exp: Initial medical management of pituitary apoplexy is 100 mg IV hydrocortisone followed by decompressive surgery. (Book p954)

items.q: What primary neuroimaging modality confirms acute intra-pituitary bleeding in suspected apoplexy?
items.exp: MRI is the investigation of choice demonstrating the pituitary bleed. (Book p954)

items.q: Sheehan syndrome is pathophysiologically defined as postpartum pituitary ___ secondary to obstetric vascular collapse.
items.exp: Sheehan syndrome is post-partum pituitary necrosis due to vascular insufficiency. (Book p954)

items.q: Which obstetric complication is NOT an established precipitating factor for Sheehan syndrome?
opts: Severe maternal hypotension and hypovolemic shock
items.exp: Precipitating factors include PPH, hypotension, DIC, shock, and multiple blood transfusions; isolated hyperemesis is not a cause. (Book p954)

items.q: A 27-year-old primigravida experiences severe uterine atony resulting in 2000 mL blood loss and hypovolemic shock requiring 6 units of PRBC transfusions. What physiological adaptation during gestation made her pituitary vulnerable to ischemic infarction?
opts: Gestational hyperplasia enlarged the gland, dramatically increasing blood flow demand
Progesterone directly induced microvascular spasm in the posterior lobe
Placental estrogen completely shut down the superior hypophyseal artery
Maternal hypercoagulability triggered primary superior sagittal sinus thrombosis
items.exp: During pregnancy, the pituitary enlarges increasing its vascular demand; obstetric blood loss produces vascular insufficiency and necrosis. (Book p954)

items.q: Match the stage in Sheehan syndrome pathogenesis to its event — 1) Normal gestation 2) Obstetric complication 3) Endocrine result … A) Pituitary enlarges increasing blood flow demand B) PPH and shock trigger severe vascular insufficiency C) Pituitary necrosis leading to hypopituitarism and hypoprolactinemia
items.exp: Pregnancy enlarges the gland; PPH triggers vascular insufficiency; necrosis yields hypopituitarism with hypoprolactinemia. (Book p954)

items.q: Assess the pathophysiology of Sheehan syndrome: I Ischemic necrosis of the postpartum pituitary is prone to secondary hemorrhage (apoplexy). II Sheehan syndrome typically results in both hypopituitarism and hypoprolactinemia.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Sheehan syndrome involves post-partum necrosis prone to bleeding into the pituitary, producing hypopituitarism with hypoprolactinemia. (Book p954)

items.q: What surgical procedure is indicated in pituitary apoplexy when neuro-ophthalmic deficits or altered consciousness fail to improve?
items.exp: Decompressive surgery is indicated following initial IV hydrocortisone in pituitary apoplexy. (Book p954)

items.q: In Sheehan syndrome, obstetric hypovolemic collapse leads to anterior pituitary infarction and ___prolactinemia.
items.exp: Lactotroph destruction in Sheehan syndrome results in hypoprolactinemia. (Book p954)

items.q: Match the intervention in pituitary apoplexy to its priority — 1) Emergency medical therapy 2) Subsequent definitive procedure … A) 100 mg IV hydrocortisone stat B) Decompressive surgery
items.exp: Immediate therapy is 100 mg IV hydrocortisone followed by decompressive surgery. (Book p954)

items.q: Why does multiple blood transfusion history often accompany the clinical records of patients with Sheehan syndrome?
opts: Reflects the severe postpartum hemorrhage and shock that precipitated pituitary ischemia
Indicates underlying chronic sickle cell hemoglobinopathy requiring lifelong exchange
Is required to treat iron deficiency anemia from chronic menorrhagia
Constitutes an autoimmune trigger that provokes lymphocytic hypophysitis
items.exp: Multiple blood transfusions and shock reflect the profound obstetric hemorrhage precipitating pituitary necrosis. (Book p954)

items.q: Assess precipitating factors of Sheehan syndrome: I Postpartum hemorrhage and systemic hypotension are classical triggers. II Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) accelerates anterior lobe infarction.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: PPH, hypotension, shock, and DIC are all recognized precipitating factors for Sheehan syndrome. (Book p954)
